---
title: Command line
description: "Inspect, check, predict, and serve saved relflow models from a shell."
---

The `relflow` executable inspects models, checks data, streams predictions,
and starts HTTP serving from a terminal, container, or scheduler. Train and
adapt models through the [Python API](training-options.qmd), then save an
artifact for prediction or serving. Keep architecture in a
[YAML template](model-templates.qmd) and supply application datasets from disk
or supported filesystem URIs. The CLI uses the same model, data-module,
processor, and tensorfield contracts as the Python API.

The executable is included in the base installation. `python -m relflow` is
equivalent. Serving requires the existing `relflow[serving]` extra, and text
encoders require their configured dependencies.

```bash
relflow --help
relflow predict --help
```

Typer generates command help, validates typed options, and provides shell
completion. Preview completion for your current shell with
`relflow --show-completion`; use `relflow --install-completion` when you want
to install it. Typer detects the current shell for these commands.

## Describe the model

Suppose each row describes one payment. The inputs are its amount and merchant;
the target is whether it was disputed. Training and validation files contain
the settled Boolean label. Request files omit the target and include a
`payment_id` for joining results.

Save this architecture as `model.yaml`:

```yaml
preset: xs
fields:
  amount:
    type: number
  merchant:
    type: category
  disputed:
    type: boolean
    mask: true
```

Inspect its resolved fields and reconstruction targets before constructing
neural modules:

```bash
relflow inspect model.yaml
relflow inspect artifacts/payment.rf --json
```

Inspection accepts templates and checkpoints. It reads declarations or saved
CPU state without creating the neural graph or initializing text encoders.
Reports include canonical addresses, masking, public outputs, preset policy,
and the producing relflow version. Stored tensor sizes include buffers; they
are not trainable parameter counts. Checkpoints use the same deserialization
semantics as `Model.load(...)`.

## Configure and check a run

Keep execution settings in a separate `predict.yaml`:

```yaml
version: 1
seed: 42
data:
  predict: payments/requests
loader:
  num_workers: 0
predict:
  batch_size: 256
  accelerator: auto
```

Local data paths in this file resolve relative to `predict.yaml`. Direct
command-line paths resolve relative to the working directory. Explicit flags
override their corresponding run settings. Unknown options, duplicate YAML
keys, and unsupported run-file versions are rejected.

Run files support `data`, `loader`, `predict`, and `serve` sections.
`data` names the `train`, `validate`, `test`, or `predict` splits and accepts a
location or a list of explicit files. Training and validation splits are
available for preflight checks. The CLI uses one device for prediction and
one HTTP server worker. Model architecture and preset options continue to
belong in the model template. Training, checkpoint resume, optimizers,
schedulers, and Trainer callbacks use Python.

```bash
relflow check artifacts/payment.rf --config predict.yaml --json
relflow check artifacts/payment.rf --config predict.yaml --execute --sample 128 --json
```

Default checks validate declarations, file discovery, and structural binding
where available without constructing the model or tensorizing source values.
Discovery can read file headers or infer text-file schemas from records.
Default binding uses a typed null observation; populated collection paths
and datatype semantics require sampled execution.
`--execute` opts into preprocessing and tensorization, with a default cap of
128 source rows. `--sample` requires `--execute`. Execution may load optional
encoders or populate configured text stores; it does not overwrite a supplied
checkpoint.

A row cap does not bound nested collections or rows emitted by processors.
Dataset-scoped preprocessing is reported as skipped by sampled checks because
it requires the full dataset. Every data phase reports its actual scope and
counts. Sampled checks cannot certify all rows or establish that task cutoffs
and splits avoid leakage. `check` is preflight; use Python
`model.validate(...)` and `model.test(...)` for evaluation.

For request data, select its prediction contract explicitly:

```bash
relflow check artifacts/payment.rf --input payments/requests --stage predict
```

## Stream predictions

```bash
relflow predict artifacts/payment.rf \
  --input payments/requests \
  --retain payment_id \
  --batch-size 256 \
  --output predictions/payment \
  --json
```

Prediction scans files through `ArrowDataModule`, writes batches through
`rf.Writer`, and avoids collecting the entire result in memory. Repeat
`--retain` to select multiple processed input columns. The canonical output
keeps `predictions`, configured `representations`, and retained `inputs`.
Preprocessors and postprocessors can change row counts, so reports distinguish
processed observations from written rows.

The default output is `rank-0.parquet`. `--format ipc` writes `rank-0.arrow`
as an Arrow IPC file, preserving sparse fixed-width vectors beneath null
containers that Parquet cannot round-trip. Both formats retain Arrow schema
metadata and require a stable schema across batches. See
[Batch inference](batch-inference.qmd).

The output directory must not exist. It includes `_metadata/` for resolved
configuration, source manifests, and job reports. Source identity uses file
metadata; source contents are not hashed. Reports record model digests, seed,
package versions, hardware, precision, and row counts.
Underscore-prefixed paths are excluded by file-source discovery, so
the directory can be read as data without including those sidecars. Consume
the complete result only after `_SUCCESS` appears. Failures retain a failed
report where possible, discard partial shards, and leave no success marker.
Choose a fresh output directory for a retry.

Automatic precision follows the SDK's hardware policy. Set
`--precision 32-true` when comparing with ordinary float32 direct inference.

## Serve a checkpoint

```bash
relflow serve artifacts/payment.rf \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --max-batch-size 128
```

This starts the existing `Deployment` HTTP runtime, including `/health`,
`/predict`, transport negotiation, and model version headers. Host binding
defaults to loopback unless configured through the command, run file, or
`RELFLOW_HOST`. Serving settings otherwise retain the deployment environment
defaults. Use the application host for ingress, authentication, and process
supervision. See [Serving](serving.qmd) for request formats and resource limits.

## Use application processors and extensions

Run files can reference installed application modules and configured processor
objects:

```yaml
version: 1
imports:
  - payments.extensions
preprocessor: payments.data:prepare
postprocessor: payments.output:warehouse
```

Extension modules are imported before schema loading. `--import` adds an
extension module from the command line. Processor references resolve to
existing decorated `rf.Preprocessor` or `rf.Postprocessor` objects; export a
`.partial(...)` object when application arguments need binding. The referenced
application package must be installed in the CLI environment.

Processor configuration is recorded alongside the run and is not embedded in
`model.rf`. Supply it again for prediction and serving when needed.
Preprocessing runs before query selection and retention; postprocessing uses
the existing output boundary.

## Automate jobs and inspect reports

Human-readable reports use Rich model trees, preflight tables, and job
summaries. Interactive terminals show a status spinner on stderr while a job
runs; redirected stderr has no live animation. Rich detects terminal color
support and respects `NO_COLOR`. Typer handles commands, flags, generated help,
and shell completion.

`--json` emits one versioned JSON object to stdout for inspection, preflight,
and finished jobs. Progress, application prints, backend logs, and debug
tracebacks go to stderr. Exit codes are `0` for success, `2` for invalid
arguments or preflight contracts, `1` for execution failure, and `130` for an
interrupt. Use `_SUCCESS` as the persisted completion signal for output jobs.

The equivalent inspection functions are available from Python:

```python
import relflow as rf

description = rf.inspect("artifacts/payment.rf")
report = rf.check(
    "model.yaml",
    data={"train": "payments/train"},
    execute=False,
)
```

Keep credentials in the filesystem backend's authentication mechanism. CLI
data locations reject embedded credentials and URI query strings so run
reports can retain source locations.
